title: The colorful star cluster NGC 2367
caption: The young open cluster NGC 2367, imaged by the MPG/ESO 2.2-meter telescope at La Silla

recognition.text: Official ESO press-release image. No published audience rating.

story: Colorful stars and gas spread across this rich view from the Wide Field Imager at ESO's La Silla Observatory in Chile. The subject is NGC 2367, a young open cluster, an infant grouping of stars.

Curiously, this youthful cluster sits in the middle of a vast, much older structure out on the edges of the Milky Way. An open cluster is a loose group of stars born together from the same cloud of gas and dust, and a young one like this can still be surrounded by some of that gas.

The cluster is a stellar infant set within something ancient. Young clusters are useful for studying how stars begin their lives, while their setting can hint at the longer history of the region around them.

understand.summary: This image from the Wide Field Imager combines U, B, V, I and hydrogen-alpha filters, from the ultraviolet end of the spectrum into the near-infrared. The color assigned to each filter isn't published.
understand.eye: Long camera exposures gather far more light than the eye can, and some of the filters record light at the edges of human vision or beyond.

behind.exposure: Not published on the source page.
behind.technique: Not stated by the source (single frame, stack, mosaic or panorama unknown).

explore: The picture was made with the Wide Field Imager on the MPG/ESO 2.2-meter telescope, combining U, B, V and I filters with one that isolates the glow of hydrogen. NGC 2367 lies in the direction of the constellation Canis Major.
alt: A rich field of colorful stars and gas.
